questions.q: Which organism is the most common cause of community-acquired pneumonia in adults?
questions.why: Pneumococcus remains the leading bacterial cause of CAP.

questions.q: A patient is found with pinpoint pupils and a respiratory rate of 6. What is the best immediate treatment?
questions.why: Miosis plus respiratory depression is the opioid toxidrome, reversed by naloxone.

questions.q: Which adverse effect is most characteristic of statins?
questions.why: Statins can cause myalgia, myopathy and rarely rhabdomyolysis.

questions.q: Metformin is contraindicated when eGFR falls below which value (mL/min/1.73 m2)?
questions.why: Metformin is contraindicated below an eGFR of 30 because of lactic acidosis risk.

questions.q: ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF most often reflects occlusion of which artery?
questions.why: Inferior STEMI is usually from the right coronary artery (sometimes a dominant circumflex).

questions.q: A 62-year-old woman has iron deficiency anemia. What is the most appropriate next step?
wrong: Oral iron and recheck in 1 year
questions.why: Iron deficiency in a postmenopausal woman is GI blood loss until proven otherwise.

questions.q: What is the best initial imaging test for suspected lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis?
questions.why: Compression ultrasound is noninvasive, accurate and first-line for proximal DVT.

questions.q: Kussmaul respirations are the respiratory compensation for which acid-base disorder?
questions.why: Deep rapid breathing blows off CO2 to compensate for metabolic acidosis.

questions.q: Which spirometry finding defines airflow obstruction?
wrong: Reduced FVC with a normal ratio
questions.why: Obstruction is defined by a low FEV1/FVC ratio; restriction lowers TLC.

questions.q: HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over roughly what period?
questions.why: Red cell lifespan makes HbA1c a measure of the preceding 2-3 months.

questions.q: At what age should average-risk adults begin colorectal cancer screening?
questions.why: US guidelines now begin average-risk screening at age 45.

questions.q: Facial twitching when the facial nerve is tapped (Chvostek sign) suggests which abnormality?
questions.why: Chvostek and Trousseau signs reflect neuromuscular irritability of hypocalcemia.

questions.q: Which patient should have one-time screening abdominal ultrasound for AAA?
questions.correct: A 68-year-old man who has ever smoked
wrong: A 68-year-old woman who has never smoked
questions.why: Screening is recommended for men aged 65-75 who have ever smoked.

questions.q: A patient with STEMI has not yet received any medication. Which drug should be given immediately?
questions.why: Aspirin has the largest early mortality benefit in STEMI; routine early beta blocker, morphine and CCB are not first steps.

questions.q: Which anticonvulsant classically causes gingival hyperplasia and hirsutism?
questions.why: Gingival hyperplasia and hirsutism are classic phenytoin effects.

questions.q: A patient on insulin is unresponsive with glucose 28 mg/dL and no IV access. What is the best treatment?
questions.why: Glucagon IM is appropriate when the patient cannot safely take oral carbohydrate and IV access is lacking.

questions.q: Which ECG finding is typical of hypocalcemia?
questions.why: Hypocalcemia lengthens the ST segment and so the QT interval.

questions.q: Which ECG finding is typical of hypokalemia?
questions.why: Hypokalemia causes ST depression, flat T waves and prominent U waves.

questions.q: Which agent reverses unfractionated heparin?
questions.why: Protamine binds heparin and neutralizes its anticoagulant effect.

questions.q: Hypotension, distended neck veins and muffled heart sounds describe which condition?
questions.why: This is Beck triad of cardiac tamponade.

questions.q: A ventilated patient suddenly becomes hypotensive with absent right breath sounds and tracheal deviation to the left. What is the next step?
wrong: Obtain a portable chest x-ray first
Order a CT of the chest
questions.why: Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis treated at once by decompression.

questions.q: Fever, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain (Charcot triad) suggest which diagnosis?
questions.why: Charcot triad indicates biliary obstruction with infection.

questions.q: Which drug class can cause angioedema without urticaria through bradykinin accumulation?
questions.why: ACE inhibitors block bradykinin degradation and can cause angioedema.

questions.q: Which diuretic is most associated with ototoxicity?
questions.why: Loop diuretics, especially at high IV doses, can cause hearing loss and tinnitus.

questions.q: What is the standard maximum time from last known well for IV thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke?
questions.why: IV alteplase or tenecteplase is given within 4.5 hours; advanced imaging can extend selected patients.
questions.review_notes: Imaging-selected extended-window thrombolysis exists; stem asks for the standard window.

questions.q: Macrocytic anemia with loss of vibration sense and ataxia suggests deficiency of which nutrient?
questions.why: B12 deficiency causes macrocytosis plus subacute combined degeneration of the dorsal columns.

questions.q: A 72-year-old has new temporal headache, jaw claudication and an ESR of 95. What is the next step?
questions.correct: Start high-dose prednisone now, then arrange temporal artery biopsy
wrong: Wait for temporal artery biopsy before any treatment
Start an NSAID and arrange outpatient MRI
questions.why: Giant cell arteritis threatens vision, so steroids start before biopsy confirmation.

questions.q: A patient on digoxin has vomiting, yellow-tinted vision, K 6.2 and complete heart block. What is the specific treatment?
questions.why: Digoxin immune Fab treats life-threatening digoxin toxicity; dialysis does not clear digoxin well.

questions.q: Which drug causes pulmonary fibrosis, thyroid dysfunction and corneal microdeposits?
questions.why: Amiodarone is iodine-rich and lipophilic, with lung, thyroid, liver and eye toxicity.

questions.q: Which lab pattern fits tumor lysis syndrome?
questions.correct: High potassium, phosphate and uric acid with low calcium
wrong: High potassium and calcium with low phosphate
Low potassium and phosphate with high uric acid
High sodium and calcium with low uric acid
questions.why: Cell lysis releases K, phosphate and purines; phosphate binds calcium.

questions.q: A cancer patient has calcium 14 mg/dL and is volume depleted. What is the first treatment?
questions.why: Volume repletion comes first; bisphosphonates follow.

questions.q: In suspected acute aortic dissection, which drug should be started first to reduce shear stress?
questions.why: An IV beta blocker lowers heart rate and dP/dt before any vasodilator is added.

questions.q: Which organism most commonly causes endocarditis in people who inject drugs?
questions.why: S. aureus, often right-sided, predominates in injection drug use.

questions.q: Which hepatitis B serology indicates immunity from vaccination only?
wrong: HBsAg negative, anti-HBs negative, anti-HBc positive
questions.why: Vaccine immunity produces anti-HBs without core antibody.

questions.q: In COPD, long-term home oxygen improves survival when resting PaO2 is at or below what level?
questions.why: Survival benefit was shown for PaO2 of 55 mm Hg or less (SpO2 88% or less).

questions.q: Which clotting factors depend on vitamin K for synthesis?
questions.why: Factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C and S require gamma-carboxylation.

questions.q: Which lab pattern fits primary hyperparathyroidism?
questions.correct: High calcium, low phosphate, high PTH
wrong: High calcium, high phosphate, low PTH
Low calcium, high phosphate, high PTH
Low calcium, low phosphate, low PTH
questions.why: PTH raises calcium and promotes renal phosphate loss.
questions.review_notes: PTH may be inappropriately normal rather than high.

questions.q: A patient took sildenafil this morning and now has chest pain. Which drug must be avoided?
questions.why: Nitrates with PDE5 inhibitors cause profound hypotension.

questions.q: A malnourished patient with alcohol use disorder has confusion, ataxia and nystagmus. What should be given first?
questions.why: Wernicke encephalopathy needs IV thiamine, ideally before or with glucose.

questions.q: Before surgery for pheochromocytoma, which drug should be started first?
questions.why: Alpha blockade comes first; unopposed beta blockade can precipitate a hypertensive crisis.

questions.q: Which finding best favors serotonin syndrome over neuroleptic malignant syndrome?
wrong: Symptom onset over one to two weeks
questions.why: Neuromuscular excitation (clonus, hyperreflexia) and rapid onset mark serotonin syndrome.

questions.q: Which is the preferred empiric first-line regimen for H. pylori infection?
wrong: PPI with amoxicillin alone for 7 days
PPI with metronidazole alone for 7 days
questions.why: Bismuth quadruple therapy is the preferred empiric regimen in current US guidance.
questions.review_notes: Newer vonoprazan regimens exist; no distractor uses them.

questions.q: Which hemodynamic profile fits cardiogenic shock?
questions.correct: Low cardiac output, high wedge pressure, high SVR
wrong: High cardiac output, low wedge pressure, low SVR
Low cardiac output, low wedge pressure, high SVR
Normal cardiac output, high wedge pressure, low SVR
questions.why: Pump failure lowers output and raises filling pressures with compensatory vasoconstriction.

questions.q: Which drug added to an ACE inhibitor and beta blocker lowers mortality in HFrEF?
questions.why: Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists reduce mortality; digoxin and loop diuretics do not.

questions.q: Which serious adverse effect is classically associated with SGLT2 inhibitors even when glucose is near normal?
questions.why: SGLT2 inhibitors can cause ketoacidosis with only modestly raised glucose.

questions.q: Which lab pattern supports hemolytic anemia?
questions.correct: Low haptoglobin, high LDH, high indirect bilirubin
wrong: Low reticulocytes, high haptoglobin, normal LDH
Low haptoglobin, low LDH, high direct bilirubin
High haptoglobin, low LDH, normal bilirubin
questions.why: Red cell destruction releases LDH and hemoglobin that consumes haptoglobin.

questions.q: Which antibody is most associated with drug-induced lupus?
questions.why: Hydralazine, procainamide and isoniazid classically cause antihistone-positive lupus.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman has pruritus, fatigue and elevated alkaline phosphatase. Which antibody is most specific for the likely diagnosis?
questions.why: This picture suggests primary biliary cholangitis, marked by AMA.

questions.q: What is the best initial screening test for hereditary hemochromatosis?
questions.why: Elevated transferrin saturation is the earliest and most sensitive screen, followed by HFE testing.

questions.q: Polyuria with dilute urine in a patient on long-term lithium most likely reflects what?
questions.why: Lithium impairs collecting-duct response to ADH.

questions.q: Erythema nodosum, ankle arthritis and bilateral hilar adenopathy in a young adult suggest what?
questions.why: Lofgren syndrome is an acute, usually self-limited form of sarcoidosis.

questions.q: Na 140, Cl 100, HCO3 15 mEq/L. What is the best interpretation?
questions.why: Gap = 140 - 100 - 15 = 25, well above normal.

questions.q: Which maneuver increases the systolic murmur of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy?
questions.why: Lower preload narrows the outflow tract and loudens the murmur; squatting and handgrip soften it.

questions.q: For an initial episode of non-severe C. difficile infection, which agent do current IDSA guidelines prefer?
questions.why: Fidaxomicin is preferred, with vancomycin an acceptable alternative; metronidazole is no longer favored.
questions.review_notes: Oral vancomycin is also acceptable; deliberately excluded from options.

questions.q: A woman with Graves disease is in the first trimester of pregnancy. Which antithyroid drug is preferred?
questions.why: Methimazole is teratogenic in early pregnancy, so PTU is used in the first trimester.

questions.q: Which test is the best initial screen for primary aldosteronism in resistant hypertension?
questions.why: The aldosterone-renin ratio screens before confirmatory testing and localization.

questions.q: Which anticoagulant is recommended for atrial fibrillation with moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis?
questions.why: DOACs were inferior to warfarin in rheumatic mitral stenosis with AF.

questions.q: A 60-year-old has had a myocardial infarction. Which lipid regimen is appropriate?
questions.correct: High-intensity statin such as atorvastatin 40-80 mg
wrong: Statin only if LDL is above 190 mg/dL
questions.why: Clinical ASCVD warrants high-intensity statin therapy.

questions.q: A patient with type 2 diabetes, eGFR 40 and albuminuria is on an ACE inhibitor. Which addition best slows CKD progression?
questions.why: SGLT2 inhibitors reduce CKD progression and cardiovascular events independent of glycemia.

questions.q: Rhomboid, weakly positively birefringent crystals in joint fluid indicate which condition?
questions.why: CPPD (pseudogout) shows rhomboid crystals with weak positive birefringence.

questions.q: Ascending weakness with areflexia follows a diarrheal illness. Which CSF finding is expected?
questions.correct: Elevated protein with normal white cell count
wrong: Normal protein with elevated opening pressure
questions.why: Albuminocytologic dissociation is typical of Guillain-Barre syndrome.

questions.q: What is the recommended treatment for neurosyphilis?
questions.why: Neurosyphilis needs CNS-penetrating IV penicillin for 10-14 days.

questions.q: Which iron-study pattern favors iron deficiency over anemia of chronic disease?
questions.why: Iron deficiency raises transferrin (TIBC) and lowers ferritin.

questions.q: Which empiric regimen is appropriate for bacterial meningitis in a 65-year-old?
questions.why: Age over 50 adds Listeria coverage with ampicillin.

questions.q: When is sustained virologic response assessed after hepatitis C antiviral therapy?
questions.why: Undetectable HCV RNA 12 weeks after therapy (SVR12) defines cure.

questions.q: What tidal volume is recommended for lung-protective ventilation in ARDS?
questions.why: Low tidal volume ventilation (4-8, target 6 mL/kg PBW) lowers mortality in ARDS.

questions.q: A patient with cirrhosis has AKI unresponsive to volume expansion and diuretic withdrawal, with a bland urine sediment. Which treatment is indicated?
questions.why: Hepatorenal syndrome-AKI is treated with albumin and a splanchnic vasoconstrictor.

questions.q: Which adjunct improves survival in cirrhosis with acute variceal bleeding, along with a vasoactive drug and endoscopy?
questions.why: Short-term antibiotic prophylaxis reduces infection, rebleeding and mortality.

questions.q: Hypercalcemia in sarcoidosis is mediated by which mechanism?
questions.why: Macrophages express 1-alpha-hydroxylase and activate vitamin D.

questions.q: Rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis with hemoptysis and linear IgG staining on immunofluorescence suggests which diagnosis?
questions.why: Linear IgG along the basement membrane is anti-GBM (Goodpasture) disease.

questions.q: Fever, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia and neurologic signs occur with a normal INR. What is the treatment?
questions.why: TTP is ADAMTS13 deficiency; emergent plasma exchange is life-saving and platelets are avoided.

questions.q: Hyperthyroidism with a very low radioactive iodine uptake is most consistent with which diagnosis?
questions.why: Stored hormone leaks from an inflamed gland while uptake is suppressed.

questions.q: A patient with HIV has Pneumocystis pneumonia and PaO2 of 60 mm Hg on room air. Which adjunct improves survival?
questions.why: Adjunctive steroids are given when PaO2 is under 70 or A-a gradient is 35 or more.

questions.q: Which lung cancer type most often causes hypercalcemia through PTH-related peptide?
questions.why: Squamous tumors secrete PTHrP, causing humoral hypercalcemia of malignancy.

questions.q: Inferior STEMI with hypotension, clear lungs and elevated JVP. What is the best initial management?
questions.why: Right ventricular infarction is preload dependent; avoid nitrates and diuretics.

questions.q: Which finding distinguishes primary from secondary adrenal insufficiency?
questions.why: Mineralocorticoid loss and high ACTH occur only in primary adrenal failure.

questions.q: Hypokalemia, non-anion gap acidosis, urine pH above 5.5 and calcium kidney stones indicate which diagnosis?
questions.why: A defect in distal H+ secretion produces high urine pH, stones and hypokalemia.

questions.q: Pneumonia with high fever, diarrhea, confusion and hyponatremia: which test gives the quickest confirmation of the likely cause?
questions.why: Legionella pneumonia is detected rapidly by urinary antigen (serogroup 1).

questions.q: A stable patient has pre-excited atrial fibrillation (irregular wide-complex tachycardia). Which drug is appropriate?
questions.why: AV nodal blockers can accelerate conduction over the accessory pathway; procainamide slows it.

questions.q: Skin necrosis in the first days of warfarin therapy reflects early depletion of which factor?
questions.why: Protein C has a short half-life so a transient procoagulant state occurs before other factors fall.

questions.q: A patient has triple-positive antiphospholipid syndrome with prior venous thrombosis. Which anticoagulant is preferred?
questions.why: DOACs carry higher thrombotic event rates in high-risk APS, so warfarin is preferred.

questions.q: Hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, hypocalciuria and metabolic alkalosis with normal blood pressure suggest which diagnosis?
questions.why: Gitelman is an inherited thiazide-like defect; Bartter causes hypercalciuria.

questions.q: A mid-diastolic rumble at the apex in severe aortic regurgitation is called what?
questions.why: The regurgitant jet impinges on the anterior mitral leaflet, causing functional mitral stenosis.

questions.q: A patient on pembrolizumab develops cough, hypoxemia and ground-glass opacities (grade 2 pneumonitis). What is appropriate?
questions.correct: Hold the drug and start prednisone about 1 mg/kg
questions.why: Moderate immune-related pneumonitis needs treatment interruption and systemic steroids.

questions.q: A 20-year-old has Coombs-negative hemolysis, acute liver failure and a low alkaline phosphatase. What is the likely diagnosis?
questions.why: Copper release causes hemolysis, and a low ALP-to-bilirubin ratio is typical.

questions.q: pH 7.20, HCO3 12 mEq/L, PaCO2 40 mm Hg. What is the best interpretation?
questions.correct: Metabolic acidosis with a concurrent respiratory acidosis
wrong: Metabolic acidosis with a concurrent respiratory alkalosis
questions.why: Expected PaCO2 = 1.5 x 12 + 8 = 26 (+/-2); 40 is too high, so ventilation is inadequate.

questions.q: In a water deprivation test, urine osmolality rises by more than 50% after desmopressin. Which diagnosis?
questions.why: A large rise after ADH analog indicates deficient ADH secretion.

questions.q: Hemolytic anemia with pancytopenia, venous thrombosis and dark morning urine. Which test confirms the diagnosis?
questions.correct: Flow cytometry for CD55 and CD59
questions.why: PNH is confirmed by loss of GPI-anchored proteins on flow cytometry.

questions.q: Pancytopenia and DIC with hypergranular promyelocytes containing Auer rods. What should be started immediately?
questions.why: Suspected APL is an emergency; ATRA is started before genetic confirmation.

questions.q: Blood culture grows yeast in a hospitalized patient. What is the best approach?
questions.correct: Start an echinocandin and remove central lines
wrong: Repeat cultures and treat only if persistently positive
questions.why: Candida in blood is never a contaminant and requires systemic antifungal therapy.
questions.review_notes: Fluconazole is an alternative in stable, azole-naive patients.

questions.q: After dapsone use, a patient is cyanotic despite oxygen, with chocolate-brown blood and normal PaO2. What is the treatment?
questions.why: Methemoglobinemia is treated with methylene blue, which reduces ferric heme.

questions.q: An early-onset hypertensive patient has hypokalemia, alkalosis, low renin and low aldosterone. Which drug targets the defect?
questions.why: Liddle syndrome is constitutive ENaC activation; ENaC blockers work and aldosterone antagonists do not.

questions.q: Palpable purpura, arthralgia, low C4 and positive rheumatoid factor point to cryoglobulinemia. Which infection is the most common association?
questions.why: Mixed cryoglobulinemia is most often secondary to chronic hepatitis C.

questions.q: Severe abdominal pain, neuropathy and psychosis follow fasting and a new antiepileptic. What is the best initial test?
questions.why: Acute intermittent porphyria is screened by urinary PBG during an attack.

questions.q: Which antibody is associated with subacute sensory neuronopathy and encephalomyelitis in a heavy smoker?
questions.why: Anti-Hu syndromes are linked to small cell lung cancer.

questions.q: Carcinoid heart disease characteristically affects which valves?
questions.why: Hepatic metabolism of serotonin spares the left heart, so right-sided plaques predominate.

questions.q: Which condition is the most common underlying cause of hepatic vein thrombosis (Budd-Chiari syndrome)?
questions.why: JAK2-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms are the leading cause.
questions.review_notes: Ranking of causes varies by series.

questions.q: Before starting carbamazepine in a patient of Southeast Asian ancestry, which HLA allele should be tested?
questions.why: HLA-B*1502 predicts carbamazepine-induced Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

questions.q: Which drug combination requires reducing azathioprine to about one quarter of the usual dose?
questions.why: Xanthine oxidase inhibition blocks 6-MP breakdown and risks severe myelosuppression.

questions.q: A patient with severe verapamil overdose has shock refractory to fluids, calcium and vasopressors. Which therapy is recommended?
questions.why: High-dose insulin improves inotropy in calcium channel blocker poisoning.

questions.q: A patient with long-standing diabetic nephropathy has hyperkalemia and mild non-gap acidosis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.why: Hyporeninemic hypoaldosteronism is the classic diabetic RTA.

questions.q: A patient from an endemic area starts high-dose prednisone, then develops gram-negative sepsis and meningitis. Which parasite is responsible?
questions.why: Steroids can trigger hyperinfection with gut bacteria translocation.

questions.q: Days after cardiac catheterization a patient has worsening AKI, livedo reticularis, eosinophilia and low complement. What is the diagnosis?
questions.why: Cholesterol emboli cause subacute stepwise decline in kidney function.

questions.q: Sodium is low and urine osmolality is 60 mOsm/kg in a patient with heavy beer intake and a poor diet. What is the mechanism?
questions.correct: Low solute intake limits free-water excretion
questions.why: Little solute for the kidney to excrete means little obligate water excretion.
questions.review_notes: Overcorrection risk when fed is the teaching point.

questions.q: Amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis with low iodine uptake and absent thyroid blood flow (type 2) is best treated with what?
questions.why: Type 2 is destructive thyroiditis and responds to steroids; thionamides are used for type 1.

questions.q: Chronic diarrhea, weight loss and migratory arthralgia are present; duodenal biopsy shows PAS-positive macrophages. Which organism is responsible?
questions.why: Whipple disease is caused by T. whipplei and treated with prolonged antibiotics.

questions.q: Which test best confirms gastrinoma when fasting gastrin is only mildly elevated?
questions.why: Gastrin rises paradoxically after secretin in Zollinger-Ellison syndrome.

questions.q: Lifelong mild hypercalcemia, family history, high-normal PTH and calcium-creatinine clearance ratio below 0.01. What is the diagnosis?
questions.why: Inactivating CaSR variants cause benign hypercalcemia with low urinary calcium.

questions.q: Which noninvasive test confirms transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis?
questions.correct: Technetium pyrophosphate scintigraphy after excluding a monoclonal protein
questions.why: Positive bone-tracer uptake with no monoclonal protein is diagnostic of ATTR.

questions.q: An elderly patient with an IgM paraprotein has epistaxis, blurred vision and engorged retinal veins. What is the emergency treatment?
questions.why: Hyperviscosity syndrome is treated by plasmapheresis; transfusion worsens viscosity.

questions.q: Which finding favors constrictive pericarditis over restrictive cardiomyopathy?
questions.correct: Respiratory variation in ventricular filling with septal bounce
questions.why: Ventricular interdependence is the hallmark of constriction.

questions.q: Recurrent venous thrombosis with minimal aPTT prolongation despite escalating heparin doses suggests deficiency of what?
questions.why: Heparin works through antithrombin, so deficiency causes heparin resistance.

questions.q: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy in a patient on natalizumab is caused by which virus?
questions.why: JC virus reactivates under impaired CNS immune surveillance.

questions.q: Rapidly progressive dementia with myoclonus. Which CSF test is most specific for the likely diagnosis?
questions.why: RT-QuIC detects prion seeding with very high specificity.

questions.q: Pancytopenia, splenomegaly, a dry marrow tap and BRAF V600E-positive cells with cytoplasmic projections. Which treatment?
questions.why: Purine analogs achieve durable remissions in hairy cell leukemia.

questions.q: Quotidian fever, evanescent salmon rash, arthritis, ferritin of 12,000 and negative ANA and RF. What is the diagnosis?
questions.why: Very high ferritin with spiking fevers and rash defines adult-onset Still disease.

questions.q: A sedated ventilated patient on high-dose propofol develops metabolic acidosis, rhabdomyolysis, hypertriglyceridemia and bradyarrhythmia. What is the diagnosis?
questions.why: Mitochondrial fatty-acid oxidation is impaired by prolonged high-dose propofol.

questions.q: Large-volume watery diarrhea, hypokalemia, achlorhydria and a pancreatic mass indicate excess of which hormone?
questions.why: This is the WDHA (Verner-Morrison) syndrome of VIPoma.

questions.q: Spontaneous Clostridium septicum bacteremia is classically associated with which underlying condition?
questions.why: C. septicum sepsis without trauma should prompt colon cancer evaluation.

questions.q: Serum sodium is 123 mEq/L, measured osmolality 292 mOsm/kg and the serum is milky (triglycerides 4000 mg/dL). What is the interpretation?
questions.why: Lipid displaces plasma water and lowers sodium on indirect measurement, with normal tonicity.
questions.review_notes: Not seen with direct ISE analyzers.

questions.q: A 28-year-old Asian man has sudden leg paralysis at night after a high-carbohydrate meal and K 2.1 mEq/L. Which test is next?
questions.why: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis shifts potassium into cells; treat the thyrotoxicosis.

questions.q: A cirrhotic patient who ate raw oysters has fever, hypotension and hemorrhagic bullae on the legs. Which antibiotic combination is recommended?
questions.why: Vibrio vulnificus is treated with doxycycline plus a third-generation cephalosporin.

questions.q: Polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, a lambda M-protein, skin changes and sclerotic bone lesions. Which cytokine is characteristically elevated?
questions.why: POEMS syndrome has markedly raised VEGF.

questions.q: A patient with short bowel syndrome has confusion, ataxia and anion gap acidosis with normal L-lactate. What is the explanation?
questions.why: The standard lactate assay detects only L-lactate.

questions.q: Hypophosphatemia and osteomalacia with normal calcium and PTH are caused by a small mesenchymal tumor. Which mediator is responsible?
questions.why: Tumor-induced osteomalacia is caused by excess phosphaturic FGF23.

questions.q: Fever, splenomegaly, pancytopenia, ferritin 30,000, high triglycerides and low fibrinogen are present. What is appropriate initial therapy?
questions.why: HLH-94 style regimens suppress the hyperinflammation; treat the trigger.
questions.review_notes: Newer agents (anakinra, ruxolitinib) are used in some centers.

questions.q: Which drug class risks precipitating pulmonary edema in pulmonary veno-occlusive disease?
questions.why: Vasodilating arterioles in a fixed venous obstruction raises capillary pressure.

questions.q: Which enzyme deficiency causes X-linked acral pain, angiokeratomas, proteinuria and left ventricular hypertrophy?
questions.why: Fabry disease causes globotriaosylceramide accumulation.

questions.q: A 70-year-old has spontaneous large ecchymoses, aPTT 80 seconds and normal PT, with no correction on 1:1 mixing and no thrombosis. What is the diagnosis?
questions.why: An autoantibody inhibits factor VIII, causing bleeding with a non-correcting aPTT.

questions.q: Primary aldosteronism is confirmed in a 45-year-old, and CT shows a 1 cm adrenal adenoma. Which test should precede surgery?
questions.why: Imaging cannot reliably lateralize aldosterone excess over age 35, so AVS is recommended.
questions.review_notes: Some centers use PET tracers; guidelines favor AVS.
